Testimony of Rep. Allison Hepler presenting
LD 1043, An Act to Provide Free Admission to State Parks and Historic Sites
for the Immediate Family Members of Veterans and Active
'
Military Personnel Before the Joint Standing Committee on Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry
Good afternoon, Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker and colleagues of the Agriculture,
Conservation and Forestry Committee. As you know, I am Allison Hepler, and I represent the towns of Arrowsic, Georgetown, Phippsburg, West Bath and Woolwich. I am pleased to present
LD 1043, An Act to Provide Free Admission to State Parks and Historic Sites for the
Immediate Family Members of Veterans and Active Military Personnel.
I'm honored to represent the two most beautiful state parks in Maine, Reid State Park in
Georgetown and Popham Beach State Park in Phippsburg. It's also an honor to represent many
veterans and their families.
Current law provides free admission to Maine resident veterans holding a lifetime park pass to state parks and historic sites. This bill would extend free admission to immediate family members.
Veterans make up nearly 10% of Maine's population, the fifth highest percentage in the nation.
Out of the 105,385 veterans, nearly half are considered from the Vietnam Era, while 15,450 have served since September ll, 2001.
For a bit of history, and a shout out to our Law and Legislative Library: Since 2004, Maine veterans have been granted free admission to state parks, and for many years their families were
also. In 2009, the bill that allowed this to happen reached its sunset clause and has yet to be
successfully reintroduced. When I introduced a version of this bill in the 13 1 st, this committee
expanded it and passed it unanimously, where it died on the Special Appropriations Table.
As many of us know, when a person serves in the military, so does the family. I first learned of this in the 1990s when I read Sarah Sn1iley's regular colunm in Maine newspapers about life as a military wife with young children. I was reminded of this reality again when I spoke with a
family a couple of years ago. That conversation prompted this bill.

District 49: Arrowsic, Georgetown, Phippsburg, West Bath and Woolwich

In conclusion, Reid and Popham are heavily used by local residents and I imagine that this is no
different from others across the state. Veterans and their families are an important part of our communities and I believe that this small token of the state's acknowledgement of their service is both reasonable and timely. Thank you for your time and I hope to be able to answer any questions you have.
District 49: Arrowsic, Georgetown, Phippsburg, West Bath and Woolwich

TESTIMONY BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON AGRICULTURE, CONSERVATION AND FORESTRY
NEITHER FOR NOR AGAINST LD 1043
An Act to Provide Free Admission to State Parks and Historic Sites for the Immediate Family Members of Veterans and Active Military Personnel
March 25, 2025
Senator Talbot Ross, Representative Pluecker, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry, my name is Andy Cutko, and I am the Director of the Bureau of Parks and Lands (BPL). I am speaking on behalf of the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF) neither for nor against LD 1043, An Act to Provide Free
Admission to State Parks and Historic Sites for the Immediate Family Members of Veterans and
Active Military Personnel.
Maine State Parks and Historic Sites currently allow free day-use access to senior citizens, children under five, Maine veterans, Gold Star families, and military service members on active duty. This bill would extend free access to Maine State Parks and Historic Sites for the immediate family members of a veteran and active military personnel, even if the veteran or
active-duty member is not present. We currently extend free access to spouses and children of
active military members, but only when that active member is present.
Because fees from State Parks are directed to the state's General Fund, this bill will have a fiscal
impact. To calculate the fiscal impact, we would need to estimate the level of State Park use by
veterans' immediate family members -- but only those family members under 65 and children
over five. We would also need to estimate state park use by active military members and their
families. Because the Bureau does not collect data on State Park use by veterans, their families, or active military personnel, the fiscal impact is difficult to estimate.
In addition, if families of veterans or active-duty members attend State Parks without the veteran or active-duty member present, the Bureau would need identification to confirm those
relationships. I understand that the Bureau of Veterans' Services is willing to verify those family
members. BPL is willing to work with Veterans' Services to create an appropriate identification
card suffieient for park entrance.
Maine veterans have provided an immeasurable service to our state and nation, and their families have made sacrifices that enabled and endured their service. Thank you for your time. I would
